system.name: Hindsight
system.one_liner: a distributed tracing system that retroactively and lazily assembles detailed traces only for requests that later prove interesting

content.subject: how Hindsight lazily collects a request's spans by triggering a coordinator's backward breadcrumb traversal instead of reporting eagerly

elements.name: traceId
elements.role: identifies the request from its first hop, same starting point as the eager baseline in Fig. 1

elements.name: traced process
elements.role: one of several processes along the request's path, each locally buffering span data

elements.name: Application
elements.role: the instrumented application code that produces span data and metadata

elements.name: Hindsight Client Lib
elements.role: buffers a process's span data and metadata locally in a ring buffer at each tracepoint

elements.name: Hindsight Agent
elements.role: indexes buffered entries and evicts old ones as the local buffer fills

elements.name: trigger
elements.role: a runtime condition that flags a request as worth tracing in detail

elements.name: Coordinator
elements.role: central service that learns of a trigger and pulls the request's earlier spans back through its breadcrumb trail

elements.name: Backend Trace Collectors
elements.role: shared backend that stores spans once they are lazily reported

relations.what: request continues hop to hop, carrying traceId; same base path as Fig. 1
span data and metadata are handed to the client library's local ring buffer
buffered entries are indexed by the agent, which evicts old ones
a runtime condition fires, flagging this request for detailed tracing
the coordinator learns of the trigger
breadcrumb traversal: the coordinator walks backward through each visited process's breadcrumb
lazy trace reporting: only spans found relevant by the breadcrumb traversal are sent

steps.what: the request is tagged with a traceId, as in the eager baseline
the client library buffers span data and metadata locally
the local agent indexes buffered entries and evicts old ones as the buffer fills
a runtime condition fires a trigger, flagging the request as worth tracing in detail
the coordinator performs a breadcrumb traversal, walking backward through each visited process

steps.at: traced processes to Backend Trace Collectors
steps.what: only the spans found relevant by the breadcrumb traversal are lazily reported

content.key_idea: Instead of reporting every span immediately, Hindsight buffers locally and only pulls a request's spans, backward through its breadcrumb trail, once a trigger flags that request as worth the cost.
content.reading_order: left to right along the request path for steps 1-3 (including the two zoomed callouts), then step 4's trigger, then backward along red breadcrumb arrows for step 5, then down to the backend for step 6

Fig. 2 shows a high-level diagram of Hindsight's main components.

summary: This figure walks through Hindsight's lazy alternative to the eager tracing design shown in Fig. 1, reusing the same wavy request-path topology through system processes. As in Fig. 1, the request is tagged with a traceId (step 1) and its spans are locally buffered; two callouts zoom into this local handling, showing the Hindsight Client Lib buffering span data and metadata at a tracepoint (step 2) and the Hindsight Agent indexing and evicting buffered entries (step 3). Later along the path, a runtime condition fires a trigger (step 4), prompting the Coordinator to perform a breadcrumb traversal (step 5): red dotted arrows trace backward through the breadcrumbs each visited process left behind, to find the request's earlier spans. Only then does lazy trace reporting (step 6) send the relevant spans to the Backend Trace Collectors, avoiding the constant eager reporting of the baseline design.
